subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification — shared vs dedicated follow-up (FinPay)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finpay.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode qualification — shared vs dedicated

Hi Alex / Sandeep,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation on expected throughput and reliability needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Summary of what I heard from the call:
  • Peak concurrency: ~200 concurrent requests during batch settlement windows (you confirmed bursty traffic).
  • Typical request size: ~3k tokens per request (average), median latency expectation: p50 < 50ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 target ~200ms for critical flows.
  • Concerns: noisy-neighbor effects on shared pools, strict isolation for payment flows, SOC 2 / audit readiness for vendor selection.

- Redwood options to consider:
  1) Hosted API (shared): fastest to get started, lower unit cost, but multi-tenant pools mean isolation is logical (rate limits/priority) rather than physical. Can meet many SLOs but higher chance of noisy-neighbor interference at extreme bursts.
  2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool for FinPay, physical isolation from other customers, configurable autoscale & burst policies. Best fit if you want deterministic performance during peak windows.
  3) Private VPC / on-prem: full network isolation, customer-managed VPCs, required for some regulated workflows. Longer lead time and procurement.

- Recommended immediate next steps:
  • Can you confirm the 200 concurrency peak and whether the payment flow requires hard p99 guarantees or something softer (SLO vs SLA)?
  • I will loop in Priyom and Vivek to map out the Dedicated sizing and isolation model for your workload.
  • I attached a short one-pager on our serving modes. I can also send a quick sizing worksheet if you want us to propose a capacity baseline and ballpark pricing.

If this captures things, I suggest a short follow-up next week to go over a Dedicated pilot plan (2–4 week pilot): baseline + runbook + success criteria.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finpay.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification — shared vs dedicated

Thanks Marissa — that looks right. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The 200 concurrency number is correct for settlement windows (30–45 minutes, once per hour). Outside those windows concurrency is < 20.
- For payment authorization flows we want hard performance guarantees around p99; incidents that cause increased latency directly affect downstream transaction timeouts.
- We are open to starting on Dedicated capacity for the mission-critical flows and using Hosted API for lower-criticality experimentation.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) How do you mitigate noisy-neighbor in shared pools today? Any historical incidents/metrics you can share?
2) For Dedicated, what isolation guarantees do we get (physical GPU allocation vs soft limits)?
3) What are the expected timelines and procurement steps for a Dedicated pilot?

Also attaching our internal procurement checklist — I can send a clean version if that helps.

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform Engineering, FinPay
alex.j@finpay.com

(Replying on behalf of Sandeep who is looping in security and infra leads.)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finpay.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification — shared vs dedicated

Appreciate the clarity, Alex — and totally hear the need for p99 guarantees on the payment path. Looping in Priyom (solutions) and Vivek (serving/runtime) to propose options below.

Short answers up front:
- Noisy-neighbor: on Hosted/shared pools we do aggressive workload-aware batching, priority queues, and prefix/KV caching to reduce contention; we also have automatic mitigation policies (request throttling, prioritized tails) but Shared is not physically isolated and can show tail variance under extreme global bursts. We can share anonymized historical metrics — will attach a short incidence summary.
- Dedicated: physical GPU pools reserved for your workload; we provide tenant isolation at the node level (no co-tenant processes), dedicated network pathing, and configurable cgroup-like resource caps per replica. This is the recommended path for strict p99 SLAs.
- Timeline: Dedicated pilot can be stood up in ~2–3 weeks after contract/PO and network setup (VPC peering / firewall rules). Pilot runs 2–4 weeks to exercise peak windows.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Priyom and Vivek produce a sizing + pilot plan using your 200 concurrency + 3k tokens/request assumptions (I attached a sizing worksheet — please fill if you want us to propose exact instance counts).
2) We share SOC 2 summary and network architecture diagram for your security team.
3) Schedule a 30-min tech deep-dive between Vivek and your infra/security folks next week.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite after we hear availability.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments:
- sizing-worksheet.xlsx (attached)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification — shared vs dedicated

Hi Alex / Marissa,

Following up with a technical recommendation based on the numbers you provided. We ran a quick capacity estimate for 200 concurrent sessions at ~3k tokens/request (bursty during a 30–45 minute window):

- Recommended pilot: Dedicated capacity with 8 x A100-class replicas (low-latency config) + autoscale headroom of +25% for unplanned bursts. This configuration gives predictable p99 latency headroom and isolates your workloads from noisy neighbors.

- Isolation details: Dedicated nodes are physically reserved (no other customers run on the same GPUs). We surface per-tenant cgroup limits, OOM protections, and per-replica CPU/network reservations. We also support route-based prioritization (payment path high priority).

- SLOs and monitoring: We can commit to an internal p99 target of <200ms for the pilot; formal SLA language and financial credits will require contract review but we can include SLO targets in the pilot runbook and measure for a 2–4 week validation.

- Network + security: We will share SOC 2 summary and a network-arch diagram (attached). For Private VPC options, we support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.

Next actions: 
1) Alex — if you can confirm procurement timeline / PO lead and a primary infra contact for the tech-deep dive, we will send a pilot plan and calendar invites.
2) Marissa — I can produce a short pilot runbook + cost ballpark based on the sizing worksheet.

Happy to jump on a call to walk the infra/security folks through isolation guarantees.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
